sections.h2: Can farmland and woodland in North Carolina be taxed at a lower use value?
sections.html:
Yes. Land that qualifies as agricultural, horticultural or forestland can be taxed on what it is worth in its current use rather than on its market value. The classes and their minimums are set in G.S. 105-277.3, and the owner has to apply with the county assessor.

Present-use value classes and their minimums
ClassMinimum land in actual productionOther test printed in the statute
Agricultural land10 acres (5 acres for an aquatic species farm, or 20,000 pounds sold a year)Average gross income of at least $1,000 over the three years before January 1
Horticultural land5 acresSame $1,000 average, with a separate income minimum for Christmas tree land
Forestland20 acres, outside any farm unitOperation under a written forest management plan

The owner also has to meet an ownership test. Land qualifies if it is the owner's residence, if the owner or a relative has held it for the four years before January 1, or if it passed from a business entity or trust that already had the classification.

sections.h2: How and when do I apply for present-use value?
sections.html:
File with the assessor in the county where the land sits. G.S. 105-277.4 sets the timing, and the main windows are short.

  • A first application is due during the regular listing period of the year the benefit is first claimed, or within 30 days of the date on a notice of changed value.
  • No fresh application is needed each year unless the land is transferred or loses eligibility through a change in use or acreage.
  • After a transfer, the new owner has 60 days from the transfer date to file, though the filing may be made at any time during the calendar year.
  • A late application needs good cause and approval from the county board of equalization and review, and it covers only that calendar year's county and municipal tax.

If the assessor decides the land no longer qualifies, the owner has 60 days from the written notice to appeal to the county board, and then may go to the Property Tax Commission. The notice must give the parcel number, the specific reason and the decision date.

sections.h2: What happens to deferred taxes when I sell use-value land?
sections.html:
The savings are a loan, not a gift. The difference between the tax on present-use value and the tax on full value is carried forward as deferred tax, and it is a lien on the land. When a disqualifying event occurs, the deferred taxes for the preceding three fiscal years become due (G.S. 105-277.4(c)).

A sale to a buyer who keeps farming or forestry can keep the classification in place. Under G.S. 105-277.3(b2), the buyer must have the land appraised at present-use value when title passes, continue the same use, file the application on time, and accept liability for the deferred taxes in writing. If the buyer does not meet those points, the taxes come due.

  • A conveyance to a government body or qualifying nonprofit at or below present-use value extinguishes the deferred lien.
  • A conveyance above present-use value makes only part of the deferred tax due, using a fraction the statute prints with the sale price less present-use value over true value less present-use value.
  • Land that leaves the program only because it entered the federal Conservation Reserve Program owes no deferred tax.

Ask the county assessor for a written statement of the deferred amount before you list the land, and give a copy to the closing attorney.

sections.h2: When is North Carolina property tax due, and when does interest start?
sections.html:
The bill is due September 1, and the cutoff for paying at face value is January 5. Interest begins on January 6 at two percent, then adds three-fourths of one percent per month or part of a month from February 1 until paid (G.S. 105-360). A postmark counts as the payment date for mail.

Your county or town may offer a discount to people who pay early, but it must adopt the schedule by resolution before May 1 and the Department of Revenue must approve it. Call the tax office to learn whether one exists this year.

sections.h2: How is a house valued, and who owes the bill if I sell during the year?
sections.html:
Assessors value a house at market value, meaning the price a willing buyer and willing seller would settle on with no pressure (G.S. 105-283). Values reset on a schedule of at most eight years under G.S. 105-286, so the number on your notice may reflect a date well before today's sales.

The person who owns the parcel on January 1 is the one listed for that tax year (G.S. 105-285). A seller who closes in spring therefore still receives the bill. Put the proration in the purchase contract and ask the closing attorney to show it on the settlement statement.

A quirk applies to land that was exempt on January 1, such as government land bought before July 1. The buyer lists it as of the acquisition date, at its January 1 true value, and it is taxed for the fiscal year starting July 1.

sections.h2: How do I contest the value on my notice?
sections.html:
Start with a hearing request to the county board of equalization and review, made in writing or in person before the board adjourns (G.S. 105-322). The board opens in April or early May in most years and runs longer in a revaluation year.

A written appeal to the Property Tax Commission follows if you lose, filed within 30 days of the date the board mailed its decision, with a copy to the assessor (G.S. 105-290). Bring sales of similar nearby homes, a contractor's repair estimate and dated photos of any defects.

sections.h2: Which relief programs apply to a home sale?
sections.html:
Three homestead-type programs exist, and an owner may use only one: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, and the income-based circuit breaker. Apply with the county assessor on Form AV-9 (NCDOR).

  • The elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • The veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 and has no age or income test (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • The circuit breaker limits tax to 4.0 or 5.0 percent of income and defers the rest (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Circuit breaker deferrals matter at sale. Deferred taxes for the previous three fiscal years come due when the owner transfers the home, so ask for the figure before closing.

sections.h2: Can I get a refund if the bill was wrong?
sections.html:
For a clerical error, an illegal tax or a tax for an illegal purpose, you can demand a release or refund in writing from the taxing unit's governing body (G.S. 105-381). A paid tax can be challenged within five years of its due date or six months of payment, whichever is later.

The body has 90 days to act. If it refuses or stays silent, a civil action against the taxing unit may be filed within three years, and a winning judgment carries 6 percent interest.

sections.h2: What if the tax is unpaid when the house sells?
sections.html:
The lien rides with the parcel. It attaches as of the listing date, with penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-355), and enforcement is a civil action in the nature of a mortgage foreclosure in the county where the land lies (G.S. 105-374).

A sale there is an auction at the courthouse door, with a deposit of up to 20 percent and a fee of up to five percent of the purchase price. Anyone may redeem before confirmation by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Ask the tax collector for a payoff figure and hand it to the closing attorney.

faqs.q: What is present-use value in North Carolina?
faqs.a: It is a way of taxing qualifying farm, horticultural and forest land on its value in its current use, not its market value. The owner applies with the county assessor, and the tax saved is carried as a lien.

faqs.q: How many acres do I need for use-value taxation?
faqs.a: Ten acres of agricultural land, five of horticultural land, or twenty of forestland in actual production. Aquatic farms have their own five-acre or 20,000-pound test, and the income test is an average of $1,000 over three years.

faqs.q: Do deferred taxes disappear when I sell farmland?
faqs.a: No. Deferred taxes for the preceding three fiscal years are due when a disqualifying event occurs. A buyer who continues the use and accepts liability in the application can keep the classification.

faqs.q: When does North Carolina property tax become late?
faqs.a: Interest starts January 6. The tax is due September 1, so a bill paid through January 5 is at face value, then two percent applies until February 1.

faqs.q: Who gets the bill if I sell in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 is listed and billed. Use the contract and settlement statement to shift the cost, and check with the tax office for the exact balance.
